---

## 2. How the Static Site Generator Works

The SSG is a three-module system: **parser** -> **generator** -> **CLI**.

### A. Entry Point — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/src/index.ts`

This is the CLI binary. It:
- Parses command-line arguments with `--content` (default `./content`) and `--output` (default `./dist`)
- Supports only the `build` command
- Calls `parseFiles()` then `generateSite()`
- Exits with error message on failure

### B. Type Definitions — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/src/types.ts`

Defines:
- **`PageFrontmatter`**: `{ title: string; date: string; tags: string[] }`
- **`PageData`**: `{ slug: string; frontmatter: PageFrontmatter; content: string; html: string }`
- **`ParseResult`**: `{ pages: PageData[] }`
- **`ParseOptions`**: `{ contentDir: string; outputDir: string }`

### C. Parser — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/src/parser.ts`

Uses **gray-matter** to extract YAML frontmatter and **marked** to convert Markdown to HTML. The flow:
1. Reads all `.md` files from the content directory
2. For each file:
   - Parses frontmatter with `matter(raw)` (gray-matter)
   - Extracts `title` (falls back to filename without `.md`), `date` (ISO format), and `tags` (string array)
   - Converts Markdown body to HTML with `marked.parse()`
   - Derives `slug` from the filename (strip `.md`)
3. Returns `{ pages: [...] }`

The `formatDate()` helper handles `Date` objects and `YYYY-MM-DD` string prefix extraction, returning empty string for missing/invalid dates.

### D. Generator — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/src/generator.ts`

Generates HTML files:
- **`wrapPage()`**: Wraps content in a minimal HTML5 boilerplate with HTML-escaped title
- **`escapeHtml()`**: Escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` characters
- **`renderIndex()`**: Creates `index.html` with all posts sorted by date descending, linking to each post's page
- **`renderPage()`**: Creates individual post pages with header (title, date, tags), main content (pre-rendered HTML), and a "Back to index" footer link
- **`generateSite()`**: Creates output directory, writes one HTML file per page, and writes `index.html`

### Note on root `index.ts`

The file at `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/index.ts` is an **unrelated Express/JWT auth API** (200 lines) — it is not part of the SSG. The actual SSG entry point is `src/index.ts`. The `tsconfig.json` compiles from `src/` to `dist/`, and `package.json`'s `bin` points to `./dist/index.js`.

### Test File — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/src/ssg.test.ts` (196 lines)

Uses a temporary directory (`.test-tmp/`) with setup/teardown helpers:
- **`setupContentDir(files)`**: Creates a temp content dir, writes given markdown files into it
- **`outputDir()`**: Returns and cleans a temp dist dir
- **`beforeEach`**: Nukes `.test-tmp/` before each test

**Test suite: `parseFiles`** (6 tests):
| Test | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Parses a single markdown file with frontmatter | Verifies slug, title, date, tags, and HTML output |
| Uses filename as title when no title in frontmatter | Fallback behavior test |
| Handles missing date and tags gracefully | Default empty values |
| Parses multiple files | 2 posts = 2 pages |
| Ignores non-markdown files | `.txt` file is skipped |
| Throws when content directory does not exist | Error handling |

**Test suite: `generateSite`** (3 tests):
| Test | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Generates index.html and individual pages | Full integration: run parser + generator, verify HTML content |
| Sorts index by date descending | Newer post appears before older post in index |
| Creates output directory if it does not exist | mkdirSync with recursive |

| **jest** (+ts-jest) | ^29.7.0 | Test framework |
| **typescript** | ^5.3.3 | TypeScript compiler |

---

## 5. Frontmatter/Template Handling

### Frontmatter is handled in `src/parser.ts` using **gray-matter**:

The expected frontmatter schema (defined in `src/types.ts`):
```yaml
---
title: Hello World
date: 2024-01-15
tags:
  - typescript
  - cli
---
```

### Existing template system (in `src/generator.ts`):

There is **no external template engine or template files**. Templates are hardcoded as JavaScript template literals:

1. **`wrapPage()`** — Base HTML shell with `<!DOCTYPE html>`, `<html>`, `<head>` (charset, viewport, title), and `<body>`
2. **`renderIndex()`** — Blog listing: header with "Blog" title, sorted articles with `<h2><a href="...">` links, date, and tags
3. **`renderPage()`** — Single post: header with title/date/tags, `<main>` with pre-rendered HTML, footer with back link

All user-submitted values go through `escapeHtml()` for XSS prevention.

### Sample content file — `/tmp/story_a7a0b9259a17/content/hello.md`:
```yaml
---
title: Hello World
date: 2024-06-01
tags:
  - blog
  - tutorial
---

This is my **first** blog post.
```

---

## Summary

This is a minimal static site generator (~140 lines of application code across 4 source files) that:
- Reads Markdown files with YAML frontmatter from a content directory
- Converts them to HTML using `marked`
- Generates a simple blog with an index page and individual post pages
- Has 9 tests covering parsing, generation, edge cases, and error handling
- Has no external template files, no CSS, and very basic HTML structure
- Uses gray-matter for frontmatter and marked for Markdown rendering
